Source-backed description section

Source: R/TosiDescriptionSection.R
TosiDescriptionSection.Rd

A read-only section contains plain source text, an optional source heading and an optional language-independent semantic type. TosiMetadata contains an ordinary ordered list of sections and owns their language and complete text extraction through $description_text(). No classification, translation or source retrieval is performed.

Types form an extensible vocabulary, not a closed enumeration. Conventions are description for an explicit general description, interpretation for source guidance, limitations for source cautions, and notes for other explanatory notices. Use a type only when a source field or heading supports it. Unfamiliar types are retained; NULL means unclassified text and does not imply that interpretation or limitations are absent. An unfamiliar heading may retain its title without a type.

Fields reject direct and nested replacement. Section instances use ordinary R6 reference semantics; metadata retains them without cloning.

Active bindings

text

Plain section text.

title

Optional source heading.

type

Optional language-independent semantic type.

TosiDescriptionSection$new()

Construct a source-backed description section.

Usage

TosiDescriptionSection$new(text, title = NULL, type = NULL)

Arguments

text

Plain section text.

title

Optional source heading.

type

Optional language-independent semantic type. No type is inferred.

Returns

A new TosiDescriptionSection object.

TosiDescriptionSection$as_list()

Project the section to ordinary R data.

Usage

TosiDescriptionSection$as_list()

Returns

A named list containing text and any supplied title and type.

TosiDescriptionSection$clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

TosiDescriptionSection$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples

section <- TosiDescriptionSection$new(
  "Survey estimates.", title = "Methods", type = "interpretation"
)
section$text
#> [1] "Survey estimates."
section$as_list()
#> $text
#> [1] "Survey estimates."
#> 
#> $title
#> [1] "Methods"
#> 
#> $type
#> [1] "interpretation"
#>
